commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Activate Zevlor by paying {2} and tapping him, then cast a spell targeting only one opponent or one opposing permanent. Each other opponent gets a separate targeted copy with identical X and choices. Preserve one-target opponent spells that multiply theft, edicts, mana, draw and hand control, with actual magecraft and legal untap support.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 4 — Optimized. Zevlor yields spectacular three-opponent spell advantage but first demands commander survival, an activation with haste and a legal one-target payload in the same turn; no reliable compact deterministic cEDH win is proved.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Keep this encyclopedia deck's targeted opponent copying, theft and response timing distinct from generic Grixis Oracle/Consultation/Breach combo; high card power alone is not enough to displace a Zevlor-specific role.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: The bound 99-physical-slot CSV audits the original October 15 source, with six mutually distinct cuts, 93 kept physical slots and all 34 lands retained. It separates one-target payloads, interaction, fast resources, magecraft/copy, untap support, tutor/card flow and land role.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Exactly 34 dedicated lands before and after, including two each of Island, Mountain and Swamp and typed Grixis duals with nine fetches. The six swaps change nonland timing: three new two-mana sorceries, four-mana Gifts, five-mana Refrain and UR X filtering make early red/black/blue needs more distinct; no extra land is silently credited.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Exchanging Abrade, Terminate and Counterspell loses instant artifact, targeted creature and counterspell coverage; Bedevil, Chaos Warp, Rakdos Charm, Deadly Rollick, Force of Will, Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Swan Song and Deflecting Swat still protect critical windows. Blasphemous Act is retained as an actual reset.

The M7 pass reopens physical opportunity costs while preserving the unique control-their-turn Worst Fears, multiple global answers and major untap synergies.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: All 99 original physical slots reexamined in the ledger; at least eleven material candidate comparisons include new October 2026 opponent-target cards, alternative tutoring, extra untaps, top-X theft, an edict role duplicate and cast-only token engine. whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: OFF-RANKING targeted 2026 printing End of the Hunt, Strategic Betrayal, Traumatic Critique and Cruelclaw's Heist; alternative Intuition, Magewright's Stone, Inside Information, Cornered by Black Mages, Blot Out and enchantment/stack protection opportunities. Each rejected card was evaluated against a real occupied slot and the six approved improvements.

It deliberately sacrifices early instant defense and black ritual speed, then stops on quality after two higher-swap exact physical portfolios lose iconic high-end theft, independent draw and mass removal.

low_swap_heightened_audit.off_ranked_opportunities: Searched beyond popular commander rankings for End of the Hunt, Strategic Betrayal, Cruelclaw's Heist, Traumatic Critique, redundant Blot Out, Intuition, additional untaps and exile-library theft. Compared with conditional cast-only Wizard value, each purchase costs a precise original role.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: An eighth-swap setup portfolio supplements Gifts with Intuition and a repeated-activation equipment line from Magewright's Stone, enabling more table-wide casts when Zevlor remains protected. Worst Fears gives a genuinely different high-end steal-a-turn option, not redundant generic draw, and Rhystic Study is commander-independent sustain against removal; the two new slots amplify existing strengths while creating worse failure states.

The nine-swap expanded theft plan adds Inside Information's X-card exile from each opposing library on top of Intuition and additional repeatability, maximizing spectacular Zevlor-multiplied resource seizures. Without Blasphemous Act the deck has no robust mass creature reset; Inside Information's temporary permission and life-cost casts do not replace surviving early attacker swarms. It inherits the alt8 loss of independent card flow and Worst Fears.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Worst Fears, Rhystic Study and Blasphemous Act are the further held incumbents in exact alt8/alt9. Their retention was earned by effect diversity, independence from the commander, and a unique emergency answer, not by avoiding more than the six selected changes.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: Broad instant answers and Gamble/Portent have high generic rate but do little with Zevlor's exclusive one-target copied-opponent effect. Moving toward six independently strong opponent-targeted payoff cards sharply raises action density once an activation resolves.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Actual physical baseline-to-final and two full higher-count source lists were audited, with 108 Scryfall Oracle records and finite test fixtures for the exact 16 original Zevlor case IDs. This confirms identity and bounded rules assumptions but does not claim empirical multiplayer win rates.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: After the sixth swap, all 93 retained noncommander physical slots were checked in the 99-slot CSV, including the 34-land count, cheap colored mana, sweepers, control-stack interaction, self-contained draw engines, activation and repeated cast/copy value. Additional credible substitutions were constructed into two entire 100-card alternatives and rejected on role-specific costs, not because six was a quota.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Intuition raises three-opponent tutoring and Kess graveyard setup, but Worst Fears delivers a distinct premium take-an-opponent-turn control payoff that makes this commander more than a repetitive library-search deck.
One additional Zevlor untap activation can produce an extra table-wide payload, but Study is vital commander-independent card advantage when removal or artifact hate prevents setup.

Copying X exiled cards from each of three enemy libraries raises burst theft, but sacrifices the only unconditional wide creature reset and exposes the vulnerable spell-copy engine to creature armies.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: An eighth-swap setup portfolio supplements Gifts with Intuition and a repeated-activation equipment line from Magewright's Stone, enabling more table-wide casts when Zevlor remains protected.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Worst Fears gives a genuinely different high-end steal-a-turn option, not redundant generic draw, and Rhystic Study is commander-independent sustain against removal; the two new slots amplify existing strengths while creating worse failure states.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: The nine-swap expanded theft plan adds Inside Information's X-card exile from each opposing library on top of Intuition and additional repeatability, maximizing spectacular Zevlor-multiplied resource seizures.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Without Blasphemous Act the deck has no robust mass creature reset; Inside Information's temporary permission and life-cost casts do not replace surviving early attacker swarms. It inherits the alt8 loss of independent card flow and Worst Fears.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: The stop is quality based: further targeted opponent tutoring via Intuition duplicates six-swap Gifts and takes Worst Fears's special turn theft; a Magewright's Stone untap consumes Rhystic Study's irreplaceable commander-independent cards; Inside Information's top-X theft costs Blasphemous Act's indispensable unconditional mass reset. Those are real improvements in best-case Zevlor activation turns but degrade the more likely disrupted and creature-heavy games. Neither complete alt8 nor alt9 earned a stronger coherent 100.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: Exactly one tagged Zevlor and 99 physical library slots, 97 distinct names, exactly six removals and six additions versus Oct15 raw approved source, Island/Mountain/Swamp each twice and all other names singleton; 34 unchanged lands, all 97 final Oracle IDs legal Grixis in 2026-10-27 snapshot.
